editorial:
Imagine your dad suddenly kicks the bucket, and you have to spend a long weekend with your weirdest relatives. That is exactly what happens to the Scanian family in this wild comedy. You get to see a bunch of eccentric people who barely like each other forced into one house while they try to deal with their grief. The vibe is like a chaotic family reunion where everyone is trying to be the favorite child, but they mostly just end up screaming at each other. It is a funny look at how family drama never really goes away, even when someone has passed on.

You will love how the actors play off each other, making the arguments feel real and hilarious. The pacing is quick, so you never get bored, though some of the jokes might feel a bit dated since it is from the nineties. If you enjoy watching people fight over small things while ignoring the big problems, you should definitely check this out. You can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look, or you can rent it on Apple TV if you just want a quick laugh. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the family discovers a secret letter from the dad that reveals he left his money to a random charity instead of them. This twist shocks everyone and actually stops the fighting because they are all equally annoyed. They realize that their bickering was pointless since there was no inheritance to win. They end the movie by hugging and finally bonding as a real family, accepting their weirdness together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dysfunctional family comedies and witty banter.
